newsitem.title: UK: Philippines hopeful of peace with rebel groups.
newsitem.headline: Philippines hopeful of peace with rebel groups.

text.p: A top Filipino official said on Thursday he was optimistic that peace would be signed with his country's last two major rebel movements after a quarter of a century of fighting.
In talks with communist rebels earlier this week in the Netherlands, House of Representatives Speaker Jose de Venecia agreed to push to conclude peace negotiations by the middle of the year.
"June 30 is a realistic date if we all work very hard," de Venecia told Reuters in an interview.
But the government must ensure it is provides economic support for the rebels and their followers once they come down from the hills, he added.
The government has been negotiating for three years to try to end the 28-year long Marxist insurgency in which more than 40,000 people have died.
Officials will hold further talks with the National Democratic Front, the communist-led umbrella group of 13 leftist organisations, next month.
"I am hopeful..we have a good chance of putting a trophy on the wall," de Venecia said.
De Venecia is himself due to meet members of a Moslem rebel group in about two weeks.
The Moro Islamic Liberation Front (MILF) is fighting for an Islamic state in the southern islands of the Philippines.
Talks so far with MILF leaders had been useful and there was a chance of a breakthrough, he said.

Since coming to power some five years ago, President Fidel Ramos has concluded peace deals with another, larger, Moslem rebel group after 24 years of fighting, and with right-wing army rebels who were linked to a spate of coup attempts in the late 1980s.
